briefing:
The domestic aggregate Airfare Price Index (APIx) registered a daily reading of 103.25 as of September 16, 2026, representing a 3.25% net expansion relative to the baseline period. This upward index movement indicates generalized price appreciation across key domestic trunk routes, reflecting resilient passenger demand and capacity-yield optimization by major airlines. The inflation was non-uniform across corridors: the Calcutta–Bombay Route Level Index (RLI) demonstrated the sharpest surge, advancing to 105.74 (+5.74%), while the Delhi–Bengaluru and Delhi–Bombay RLIs recorded more moderate gains, reaching 102.97 (+2.97%) and 101.60 (+1.60%) respectively. Weighted at 40% for Delhi–Bombay and 30% each for Delhi–Bengaluru and Calcutta–Bombay, the aggregated figures point toward broader firming in passenger transport tariffs across primary metro pairs.

A granular breakdown of advance booking windows reveals that medium-term forward pricing, particularly the 30-day horizon (T+30), served as the primary engine of index inflation. On the Calcutta–Bombay route, the T+30 median fare spiked by 50.02%, escalating from a base median of ₹9,138 to a target median of ₹13,709, yielding a price relativity of 150.02% and contributing 30.00 points directly to that route's index. Similarly, Delhi–Bengaluru saw its T+30 median advance by 12.59% (from ₹8,829 to ₹9,941) alongside a 4.73% rise in its T+15 window (from ₹9,286 to ₹9,725.5), easily neutralizing a 14.28% contraction in its immediate spot (T+1) fare window. On the Delhi–Bombay corridor, T+30 and T+45 booking windows both converged upward to ₹7,019 from base medians of ₹6,530 (+7.49%) and ₹6,684 (+5.01%), underscoring steady forward curve hardening across all monitored sectors.

Analysis of the granular scraped ticket inventory reveals significant inter-carrier pricing dispersion and structural shifts introduced by secondary airport hubs. For example, during the high-inflation T+30 window on the Calcutta–Bombay route, low-cost carriers like Akasa Air offered entry fares at ₹9,382 into Navi Mumbai (NMI) and SpiceJet listed non-stop flights at ₹10,008, whereas market leader IndiGo priced its direct prime-time inventory significantly higher, reaching ₹18,405 (6E-5227) and ₹17,250 (6E-5128), which pushed the route's overall median upward. Furthermore, the inclusion of regional secondary airports introduced noticeable price variances: on the Delhi–Bombay corridor at T+7, Akasa Air offered a deal fare of ₹4,860 departing from Noida International Airport (Jewar - DXN), creating a substantial discount relative to the standard ₹6,530 baseline non-stop fares operating out of Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL).

Looking forward, the acute price pressure concentrated in the 30-day advance booking window—corresponding to travel mid-October 2026—signals an early buildup in seasonal and festive travel demand. From a monetary policy standpoint, this forward curve steepening indicates potential transitory inflationary spillovers into the transport and communication sub-group of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). While near-term spot fares remain relatively bounded, sustained elevated forward medians across trunk corridors warrant continued close monitoring by policy makers to evaluate core service inflation persistence and assess the degree to which secondary airport infrastructure expansion can absorb overflow demand to moderate aggregate yield volatility.
